title: Directors' Incentives from Potential Penalties: Evidence from Their Voting
eligible_reason: Table 2 columns (3) and (5) are control-free staggered TWFE regressions: reghdfe has_diss treated, a(firm_year_fe director_fe) [col 3] or a(firm_quarter_fe director_fe) [col 5], vce(cluster firm_fe) keepsingletons, on a director x firm x quarter voting panel of Chinese listed firms (2004Q1-2019Q4). `treated` ('Connection penalized') is a 0/1 indicator that switches on in the month (sor_year_month) a director connected to the focal independent director through a shared board receives a regulatory penalty, and stays on; in the shipped data treated equals 1[mdiff >= 0] exactly (mdiff = months relative to the source penalty), with 94 distinct event months in 18 years (2002-2019), 612 ever-treated directors (91 already treated at sample start) and 16,659 never-treated directors. Unit FE = director; calendar-time FE = firm x year (col 3) or firm x quarter (col 5). FLAG for the lead: the time FE are interacted with the firm of the observation, and directors sit on several boards simultaneously (mean 1.26, max 7 firms per director-quarter), so firm is not strictly a time-invariant director characteristic; the project precedent (mnsc.2023.4795, worker-level specs with firm x quarter FE) recorded such specs as eligible with a flag, and I follow it. All other main-text columns add time-varying director or firm controls (Table 2 cols 1, 2, 4, 6), add severity-split treatment regressors treated2_2 / treated3_3 (Table 4), or interact treated with moderators (Tables 5b, 6). Figure 3 (yearly binned event study) and Figure 4 (Sun-Abraham eventstudyinteract, cohort(sor_year), control_cohort(never-treated)) both include the director controls, so they are near-misses only. Table 3 (firm-level, dum_treated = board has at least one treated director) is not an adoption design: in the shipped data 479 of 1,312 ever-treated firms switch off and 381 switch more than once, and the outcome is a placebo (firm penalized). IMPORTANT: the shipped reg.dta is a pseudo dataset (README: continuous variables replaced by normal draws, has_diss replaced by Bernoulli draws with the same mean), so published estimates cannot be reproduced; the treatment/timing/FE variables appear real but the outcome is noise.
design_notes: Replication/: README.md, code/main.do (Tables 2-6, Figure 3 data, Figure 4), code/main.ipynb (Figures 1-3 plots), data/reg.dta (346,088 director-firm-quarters, 36 vars, 17,271 directors, 3,493 firms), data/reg_firm.dta (49,347 firm-years, 4,041 firms, 1991-2021), figure1.parquet, figure2.parquet. Output folder with published results is NOT in the archive (README says it is in the online version). Panel structure verified: exactly one row per PersonID x firm_fe x (year, quarter). Variables: has_diss 'Director has dissension in this firm-quarter' (binary, LPM); treated 'Connection penalized'; sor_year_month 'Month of source penalty' (constant within director); mdiff 'Month relative to source penalty' (-186..181); firm_year_fe, firm_quarter_fe, director_fe, firm_fe, year_fe precomputed group ids; treated2_2 / treated3_3 = connection penalized for top-50% / top-33% severe penalties; director controls second_term ln_tot_w prior_ind_w prior_exe_w ln_salary_w; firm controls sizew cash_ratiow roa_ebitw lev_ratiow; moderators high_cov low_vol d_ties tie_gender alumni any_tie. Figure 4 code references sor_year and sor_quarter which are absent from reg.dta (would need to be derived from sor_year_month). Sample 2004-2019 (64 quarters). Commercial sources (CSMAR/WIND-type Chinese databases) 'described in the manuscript'; contact [email removed].
n_eligible_specs_note: Table 2 col 3 (firm x year FE) and col 5 (firm x quarter FE). Both flagged for the firm-of-observation x time FE issue. Figure 3 and Figure 4 become eligible if the director controls are dropped (near-misses).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 94 distinct sor_year_month (18 distinct years, 2002-2019) among the 930 directors with an event in reg.dta; 612 directors are ever treated within 2004-2019 and 521 of them have pre-treatment quarters; 91 are always treated (event before sample start). Monthly timing variables appear to be original (README randomized only continuous variables and has_diss).
never_treated_note: 16,659 of 17,271 directors never treated (Figure 4 uses them as control_cohort).
modern_estimators_named: sun_abraham (eventstudyinteract, Figure 4, cohort(sor_year), control_cohort(never treated), covariates(director controls), window -5..+5 years)

priority_note: Eligible design with two control-free TWFE columns and a Sun-Abraham figure, but the shipped outcome is random noise; real director-voting and penalty data come from commercial Chinese databases and must be requested from the authors ([email removed]). Published coefficients are not in the package.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Full-text flags: Goodman-Bacon, staggered, Sun and Abraham, TWFE; cites Baker-Larcker-Wang. Judgement calls for the lead: (1) firm-of-observation x year/quarter FE with director unit FE (multi-board directors) - recorded eligible with flag per precedent; (2) 91 always-treated directors in the pseudo data; (3) outcome is a binary LPM at the director-firm-quarter level (repeated observations per director-quarter across boards). Eligibility and table numbering must be re-checked against the published article.
